artifacts.name: figure-1-p02.png
artifacts.caption: Figure 1: Overall pipeline of AgentJudgeBench. Each BFCL-style Agentic record undergoes difficulty-controlled rewriting, generator inference, and parallel scoring by a programmatic judge and LLM judges (with/without GT), followed by alignment with the programmatic reference.

artifacts.name: figure-2-p05.png
artifacts.caption: Figure 2: Evaluation pipeline of AgentJudgeBench. Records expand into three difficulty tiers, LLM judges (with/without GT) and programmatic judge score the generated tool-call predictions.

artifacts.name: table-1-p07.png
artifacts.caption: Table 1: Full C3 results on Llama-3.3-70B generator. All values are mean alignment (%) over 3,764–3,771 records per cell. cGT: corrupted-GT condition. Gemini: Gemini 2.5 Pro. ∆cGT-GT: corrupted-GT minus standard GT. ∆cGT-noGT: corrupted-GT minus without GT.

artifacts.name: table-2-p07.png
artifacts.caption: Table 2: LLM–judge alignment (%) with the program- matic reference across generators, judges, difficulty, and GT condition. Bold = column-wise maximum within each generator block among the six main judges. Prom2 = Prometheus-2, a judge-specialised baseline (Limita- tions); shown for reference and not counted toward bold column-wise maxima or six-judge statistics. full breakdowns are in Appendices

artifacts.name: figure-3-p08.png
artifacts.caption: Figure 3: Per-metric alignment (with and without GT) across the six main judges, plus Prometheus-2 (judge- specialised baseline; Limitations), shown for reference.

artifacts.name: table-3-p08.png
artifacts.caption: Table 3: Pairwise inter-judge agreement under the with GT condition. Upper triangle : exact metric-level

artifacts.name: table-4-p08.png
artifacts.caption: Table 4: Hard without GT alignment (%) under the standard 1.0-default and the recalibrated 0.5-default prompts, averaged across six judges per generator. ∆= (0.5-default) −(1.0-default).

artifacts.name: figure-4-p09.png
artifacts.caption: Figure 4: Judge temperature sensitivity. Qwen3-32B alignment at T ∈{0.3, 0.7, 1.0} on Llama-3.3-70B. All three difficulty curves are near-flat; maximum spread ≤0.6 pp.

artifacts.name: figure-5-p09.png
artifacts.caption: Figure 5: Prompt structure vs. alignment. Structured JSON prompt vs. free-form for Qwen3-32B on Llama- 3.3-70B. The per-metric rubric adds +4.8-+6.5 pp with GT across all difficulty levels.

artifacts.name: table-5-p09.png
artifacts.caption: Table 5: Chain-of-thought reasoning in the QwQ-32B judge: alignment (%) with thinking on vs. off across four open-weight generators. ∆= thinking-on − thinking-off (pp).

artifacts.name: table-6-p13.png
artifacts.caption: Table 6: Best judge per deployment scenario. The with- out GT rows reflect the common deployment setting where ground-truth tool calls are unavailable. GT = ground-truth tool calls available; without GT = judge uses only query and tool schemas. Alignment (%) is unweighted mean over five generators.

artifacts.name: figure-6-p15.png
artifacts.caption: Figure 6: DAG topology distribution across the 3,808 unique records (left: proportional pie, right: absolute counts). Fan-in accounts for over a quarter of all records; loop-like is the rarest at 5.9%.

artifacts.name: table-7-p15.png
artifacts.caption: Table 7: Record counts by DAG topology. Counts reflect unique records; each record has three difficulty variants (easy / medium / hard), giving 3,808×3 = 11,424 total rows in the full dataset.

artifacts.name: figure-7-p15.png
artifacts.caption: Figure 7: Frequency distributions of (left) available tools per record, (centre) parameters per tool, and (right) expected tool calls per record. Dashed vertical lines mark the mean of each distribution. Tool inventory is tightly concentrated around 13 (range 8-19); parameter counts are right-skewed with a median of 2; expected call-sequence length ranges from 2 to 5.

artifacts.name: table-8-p15.png
artifacts.caption: Table 8: Structural statistics of the 3,808 Agent- JudgeBench records. All quantities are computed over unique records (collapsing difficulty variants). Avail- able tools is the size of the tool inventory exposed to the generator per record. Parameters per tool counts typed argument fields in each tool’s JSON schema. Expected tool calls is the length of the ground-truth execution trace.

artifacts.name: table-9-p16.png
artifacts.caption: Table 9: Number of records with valid LLM-judge ver- dicts per generator and difficulty tier. Theoretical max per generator is 3,808 × 3 = 11,424 (three difficulty variants of each base record). Judged records are iden- tical across all six LLM judges for a given (genera- tor, difficulty) cell. Multiplying the Total column by 6 judges × 2 conditions yields the full evaluation in- stance count per

artifacts.name: table-10-p17.png
artifacts.caption: Table 10: Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals for alignment (%) on the Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct generator. Format: mean [lo, hi].

artifacts.name: figure-8-p17.png
artifacts.caption: Figure 8: Mean judge alignment as a function of query difficulty, averaged across all six judges and five gen- erators. The without GT degradation slope is roughly 1.5× steeper than the GT slope across all generators.

artifacts.name: table-11-p17.png
artifacts.caption: Table 11: Generator programmatic accuracy ¯p (%) on AgentJudgeBench, averaged across the four metrics and six DAG topologies. Generators are ranked by hard- difficulty accuracy.

artifacts.name: table-12-p17.png
artifacts.caption: Table 12: Human annotator agreement with the program- matic scorer across 120 hard-difficulty records (n=480 metric-level verdicts), stratified at 20 records per DAG topology.

artifacts.name: table-13-p18.png
artifacts.caption: Table 13: Judge alignment (%, with GT) on 120 hard records: vs. programmatic reference and vs. human verdicts (35 corrected). ∆= human −programmatic. Smaller |∆| is better.

artifacts.name: table-14-p19.png
artifacts.caption: Table 14: With-GT judge ranking (programmatic ref- erence) under alternative weightings of the parameter- structure metric. The full six-judge ranking is identical across all three weightings.

artifacts.name: table-15-p19.png
artifacts.caption: Table 15: With-GT alignment (%) under the current parameter-structure rule vs. the maximally generous upper-bound correction, record-weighted across the full corpus. Judges’ own verdicts are held fixed; only the programmatic reference’s parameter-structure score changes. Ranking order is identical to the current one in both columns.

artifacts.name: table-16-p22.png

artifacts.name: table-17-p22.png
artifacts.caption: Table 17: Comparison of systems that deploy LLM judges for agentic tool-calling evaluation. Judge Model: LLM used as judge. Per-Metric: whether evaluation is decomposed into fine-grained dimensions. Difficulty: whether tasks span multiple difficulty tiers. GT Abl.: whether the effect of ground-truth availability is studied. Prog. Ref.: whether a deterministic evaluator is used as a bias-free basel

artifacts.name: table-27-p26.png
artifacts.caption: Table 27: Judge temperature sensitivity, second pairing: with-GT alignment (%) for GPT-OSS-120B on Llama- 3.1-8B-Instruct. Maximum spread (0.25 pp) is even tighter than the original (Qwen3-32B, Llama-3.3-70B) pairing in Table 25 (≤0.6 pp), confirming temperature insensitivity generalises beyond the original test-bed cell.

artifacts.name: table-28-p26.png
artifacts.caption: Table 28: Judge alignment (with GT, %) by DAG topol- ogy. Bold marks the best judge per topology.

artifacts.name: figure-9-p26.png
artifacts.caption: Figure 9: Judge alignment (%) by DAG topology (with GT), visualised as a heatmap. Fan-out consistently achieves the highest alignment across all judges; fan-in and loop-like are the hardest. The ordering is judge- independent, indicating that DAG structural complexity is an intrinsic difficulty signal.

artifacts.name: figure-10-p27.png
artifacts.caption: Figure 10: Verdict-level confusion matrices (% of N). Rows = judge 1, columns = judge 2. Diagonal entries are shaded.
